intervals.note: Start verified (October 2010). Open interval: no source read states when the WIPP run ended or that it continues. The latest DMTPC paper read is arXiv:1705.05965 (2017), a model of directional sensitivity of two DMTPC laboratory detectors; no WIPP dark matter result was found. The 2021 Annual Review (arXiv:2102.04596) describes DMTPC only in the past tense and says 'A 1 m3 detector was constructed, but to our knowledge not deployed'. The collaboration website's last Internet Archive capture is 2019-07-29.

physics_goals.quote: The Dark Matter Time Projection Chamber (DMTPC) experiment uses CF_4 gas at low pressure (0.1 atm) to search for the directional signature of Galactic WIMP dark matter.
physics_goals.value: Directional detection of WIMP dark matter with a low-pressure CF4 gas TPC

summary.plain: DMTPC (Dark Matter Time Projection Chamber) is a directional dark matter experiment led from MIT. A low-pressure CF4 gas chamber with camera readout images the tracks of recoiling nuclei, which could reveal the direction a dark matter particle came from. A 10-litre detector ran at MIT and then underground at WIPP.
summary.technical: Low-pressure (75 Torr) CF4 dual back-to-back TPC with CCD (proportional scintillation) and charge readout, 10-liter detector with a 3.3 g CF4 target. MIT surface run (35.7 g d, 80-200 keV): spin-dependent WIMP-proton limit 2.0e-33 cm^2 at 115 GeV/c^2 (90% CL). Moved to the Waste Isolation Pilot Plant (1.6 km w.e.) in October 2010; a 20-liter detector was commissioned at MIT. 2017: model of the directional response of two detectors at 30-60 torr.
